rationale: This uses exactly the same three ingredients as the archive's best performer "ExternalFunding CashDrain AccrualStrain" (accrual gap × [net external financing − cash change]) with only SUB swapped for MIN, which is a cosmetic operator variant rather than a new mechanism, and the MIN form is already represented in the archive ("DebtFunded Payout CashShortfall").

The dp add-back genuinely re-specifies the accrual leg toward working-capital accruals and the cash-retention condition is a defensible sharpening of the weak archive "NonDepreciationAccrual DebtIssuer," though the mechanical link between oancf in the accrual leg and DELTA(che) in the financing leg (che change ≈ oancf + ivncf + fincf) risks a partly tautological interaction.

The profitability screen is a sensible guard against a loss-firm financing artifact and is consistent with the stated hypothesis, but nesting two MINs of ranks heavily compresses the signal into whichever single leg is lowest, so the "conditional" logic may degrade into a noisy min-rank rather than a true interaction.

Replacing oancf with DELTA(che) in the archive's "WorkingCapitalBuild FinancingDeficit" is a substantive change of the funding-use benchmark (retained liquidity vs. operating cash generation) rather than a rescaling, the sign conventions are internally consistent, and it plausibly inherits the strongest archive mechanism—but it remains an incremental one-term substitution on an already-tested signal.

Beyond being a triple-MIN restatement of the archive's "DebtFunded Payout CashShortfall," the payout leg is now a raw level rank whose unconditional cross-sectional sign is positive (high payout firms are typically profitable, low-risk), so requiring high payout as a bearish condition works against the hypothesis and the three-way MIN further collapses the signal to a single compressed order statistic.

This is the archive's "PostFunding AccrualDeterioration" with a cash-change term appended to the lagged leg; that parent already showed a decent FMB t-stat but a wrong-signed, insignificant portfolio alpha, and the proposal offers no diagnosis of that cross-sectional/portfolio divergence to justify why this minor addition would fix it.
